papers.title: Circadian Oscillation Detection Analysis and Comparison (CODAC): a Multicriteria Method to Estimate and Compare Rhythmicity
papers.summary: CODAC is a multicriteria framework for circadian rhythm detection that integrates nonlinear constrained optimization and avoids single p-value cutoffs. It provides modules for single-group, flexible waveform, pairwise, and multi-group comparisons, showing performance comparable to established methods with added flexibility.

papers.title: α5-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors regulate state transitions in cortical networks and modulate susceptibility to epileptiform discharges.
papers.summary: This study investigated the role of α5-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in regulating cortical state transitions and epileptiform discharges. Using acute brain slices from wild-type and α5 knockout mice, the authors found that α5KO networks exhibited slower spontaneous activity and tolerance to high-amplitude spike-and-wave discharges, suggesting a critical role for α5-nAChRs in cortical excitability and ictogenesis.

papers.title: Propofol-Facilitated Recovery Sleep Modulates Cognitive Function via Slow Oscillation-Spindle Coupling After Acute Sleep Deprivation in Rats.
papers.summary: In a rat model, propofol-facilitated recovery sleep after acute sleep deprivation improved spatial and recognition memory, increased slow oscillation density, and strengthened phase-accurate SO-spindle coupling, accompanied by reduced cortical NKCC1/KCC2 ratio.

papers.title: Optogenetic activation of parabrachial tachykinin1 neurons drives nonphotic circadian entrainment
papers.summary: The study identified a neural circuit for nonphotic circadian entrainment: optogenetic activation of parabrachial tachykinin1 neurons recapitulated foot-shock-induced phase shifts in mice, with projections to the central amygdala (CeA) partially mediating the effect and requiring an intact CeA molecular clock (Bmal1).

papers.title: Juvenile AAV-Mediated MEF2C Gene Replacement Ameliorates Selected Phenotypes in Mef2c-Haploinsufficient Mice
papers.summary: This study tested juvenile AAV-mediated delivery of MEF2C isoforms in Mef2c-haploinsufficient mice, finding improvements in social novelty, sleep, and selected brain measures, indicating modifiable phenotypes during the juvenile period.

papers.title: Enriched experience increases reciprocal synaptic connectivity and coding sparsity in higher-order cortex.
papers.summary: In mice, 10 weeks of enriched environment increased bidirectional excitatory synaptic connections in higher-order cortex and sparser, more orthogonal population activity during rest and sleep, supporting attractor network predictions.

papers.title: Distributed state-dependent neural ensembles across sleep stages
papers.summary: This study mapped neural activity across >40 brain regions in mice, revealing a distributed sleep code with slow and fast timescale dynamics, including state transitions and nested oscillations, and identified regional covariation with neuromodulatory innervation.

papers.title: Neural and behavioral correlates of consciousness: the welfare consequences of fatal hypobaric and hypercapnic hypoxia in laboratory mice.
papers.summary: This study compared neural and behavioral responses in laboratory mice during hypobaric and hypercapnic hypoxia-induced unconsciousness, finding that hypobaric hypoxia produces an early shift to delta frequency bands indicative of an anesthetic-like state and reduced capacity for negative experiences. This suggests hypobaric hypoxia may be a more humane euthanasia method.

papers.title: Rapid associative spine enlargement is required for cognitive function and stable wakefulness
papers.summary: The authors developed SynC, a chemogenetic tool that selectively blocks rapid associative spine enlargement in mouse neocortical neurons. Acute inhibition of spine enlargement impaired cognitive behaviors and reduced pairwise spike correlations during wakefulness, while sparing baseline firing and gamma activity, indicating that rapid spine enlargement is required for stable awake cognition.

papers.title: Maternal sleep deprivation reshapes offspring hippocampal development through a Trem2-centered microglial program revealed by single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.summary: Using single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics in rats, this study showed that maternal sleep deprivation during late pregnancy causes cell-type-specific transcriptional changes in offspring hippocampus, with persistent microglial disruption centered on Trem2 downregulation, associated with behavioral and synaptic deficits that were partially rescued by hippocampal Trem2 restoration.

papers.title: Inkjet-Printed Aqueous Graphene Suspensions on Flexible Substrates for Multimodal Wearable Continuous Health Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of inkjet-printed graphene electrodes on PET substrates for wearable health monitoring. The electrodes showed high conductivity, flexibility, and reusability, and successfully recorded ECG, EEG, EOG, and EMG signals with high correlation to gel-based commercial electrodes, demonstrating potential for practical applications.

papers.title: Predicting Anxiety Trajectories from Individual Differences in Sleep-Related Distress Alleviation
papers.summary: This cohort study investigated whether individual differences in REM sleep-related overnight distress alleviation predict anxiety recovery. In 223 adults with insomnia and psychiatric symptoms, stronger REM-related distress alleviation at baseline predicted greater anxiety improvement after two months, independent of treatment, suggesting a link between REM sleep emotion regulation and anxiety recovery.

papers.title: The Human Intracerebral EEG Platform: A Cloud-Based Trusted Research Environment for Collaborative SEEG Research in Epilepsy and Neuroscience.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and implementation of the Human Intracerebral EEG Platform (HIP), a cloud-based trusted research environment for collaborative SEEG data sharing and analysis, now hosting 34 institutions and 10 projects.

papers.title: Sleep microstructure and cognitive trajectories in healthy aging: Insights from a longitudinal cohort study.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of older men found that baseline sleep microstructure measures (spindles, slow waves, EEG coherence) were associated with concurrent cognition and ten-year cognitive change, suggesting they may serve as markers of cognitive resilience or decline.

papers.title: Low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (0.5-5 Hz): effects on EEG band amplitude, interhemispheric coherence, and cognitive performance.
papers.summary: This double-blinded crossover study in 17 healthy adults examined the effects of low-frequency anodal transcranial pulsed current stimulation (tPCS) at 0.5, 1, 3, 5 Hz and sham on EEG and cognitive performance. The results showed frequency-dependent modulation of EEG coherence and power (e.g., 1 Hz increased coherence, others reduced power) but no significant changes in reaction time or error rates.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment alleviates chronic unpredictable stress-induced cognitive dysfunction in male rats and is associated with alterations in BDNF/TrkB signaling.
papers.summary: The study investigated whether environmental enrichment (EE) alleviates chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced cognitive dysfunction in male rats and examined associated BDNF/TrkB signaling and neuroinflammation. EE improved recognition memory impaired by CUMS and attenuated stress-induced increases in corticosterone and inflammatory cytokines, decreases in BDNF/TrkB, and oxidative stress markers.

papers.title: Normative Modeling of EEG Complexity Reveals Cortical Rigidity Associated with Pain Severity in Chronic Pain.
papers.summary: This study applied normative modeling to EEG complexity (Higuchi fractal dimension) in chronic pain patients. Larger negative deviations from healthy norms, particularly in frontal regions, were significantly correlated with higher pain intensity, suggesting that normative deviation mapping of EEG complexity could serve as a marker for chronic pain severity.

papers.title: EFS-NET: EEG-fNIRS multi-scale fusion network based on spatial calibration.
papers.summary: The authors propose EFS-Net, an end-to-end multi-scale fusion network combining EEG and fNIRS with spatial calibration, which outperforms unimodal and traditional fusion models on two public datasets, achieving up to 81.69% accuracy.

papers.title: Amphetamine-type stimulants in young adults with ADHD: effects on sleep, circadian rhythms, and neuropsychiatric outcomes.
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes literature on amphetamine-type stimulant use, sleep, circadian rhythms, and neuropsychiatric outcomes in young adults with ADHD, highlighting how stimulant pharmacology interacts with circadian system and sleep to potentially increase susceptibility to circadian misalignment and sleep disruption.

papers.title: Abnormal local markers of sleep homeostasis in patients with focal epilepsy.
papers.summary: In patients with focal epilepsy, high-density EEG showed higher slow-wave activity and steeper slow-wave slopes compared to controls, with local theta extremes discriminating patients (AUC=0.84), and left-lateralized epileptiform discharges were associated with reduced overnight slow-wave decline.

papers.title: Multidimensional Microstate Alterations and Interpretable Classification of Electrical Status Epilepticus During Sleep Using Multi-Channel EEG.
papers.summary: The study developed a microstate-based EEG framework identifying ESES-related alterations in microstates B and C, with reduced flexibility and increased regularity, and a five-feature logistic regression model achieved promising classification accuracy.

papers.title: Plasma ALKBH5 depletion during severe intermittent hypoxia and its attenuation by galectin-3 inhibition: an experimental rat study.
papers.summary: In rats, severe intermittent hypoxia reduced plasma ALKBH5 levels, while galectin-3 inhibition with modified citrus pectin attenuated this reduction and reduced hypoxia-induced myocardial injury.

papers.title: Altered early cortical EEG maturation and its relationship to language development in Down syndrome
papers.summary: This study analyzed longitudinal resting-state EEG and developmental data from children with Down syndrome (DS) and typically developing controls, finding altered cortical maturation trajectories in DS, including a decreased aperiodic exponent with age and limited alpha maturation, with a spectral dimension associated with verbal developmental quotient independent of chronological age.

papers.title: Sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems: an overnight non-invasive EEG study.
papers.summary: The study used a non-invasive EEG mask to compare sleep architecture and lying behavior in horses across age groups and two housing systems over four nights, finding significant differences in sleep stages and lying behavior between systems and age groups, with younger horses showing more REM sleep and longer lying episodes. These findings suggest that housing conditions and age should be considered when assessing equine sleep and well-being.

papers.title: Perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation and EEG biomarkers of sleep improvement after gynecologic laparoscopy: protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized controlled trial testing whether perioperative transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) reduces postoperative sleep disturbance incidence after gynecologic laparoscopy, with continuous EEG monitoring to explore mechanistic biomarkers.

papers.title: Insomnia Increases Susceptibility to Sciatica: Evidence from Mendelian Randomization and Integrative Genetic Analyses.
papers.summary: Using Mendelian randomization and integrative genetic analyses, this study found a causal effect of insomnia increasing sciatica risk (OR 3.15), with genetic correlation and prioritized candidate genes EIF3KP1 and PPIP5K2, suggesting central nervous system mechanisms.

papers.title: Genetic and stochastic basis of phenotypic discordance in 16p11.2 mouse model deletion.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study examined phenotypic discordance in a 16p11.2 deletion mouse model, finding that ~50% of isogenic del/+ mice show high seizure susceptibility to pentylenetetrazole. High responders exhibited distinct circuit activation, reduced cortical volume, sleep disturbances, and altered gene expression, suggesting convergent molecular and structural signatures underlying variable expressivity.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic effects of combined sleep-circadian interventions on depressive symptoms and sleep outcomes in adults with mental disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 RCTs assessed the effects of combined sleep-circadian interventions on depressive symptoms and sleep outcomes in adults with mental disorders, finding significant improvements in depressive severity, insomnia, sleep quality, and functional impairment, though evidence certainty ranged from very low to moderate. The results provide promising transdiagnostic evidence for these interventions.

papers.title: Contemporary Sedation Strategies for Mechanical Ventilation: Balancing Patient Outcomes, Delirium Prevention, and Early Recovery.
papers.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
papers.summary: This review discusses contemporary sedation strategies for mechanically ventilated patients, highlighting a shift from deep sedation to lighter protocols with daily interruptions and spontaneous breathing trials to reduce delirium and ICU-acquired weakness. It covers pharmacological options, monitoring techniques, and implementation frameworks like the ABCDEF bundle, emphasizing non-pharmacologic interventions and tailored approaches for special populations.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of gut health, inflammatory factors, and sleep quality among shift workers: A cross-sectional study.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 200 shift workers found that night-shift workers had significantly more gastrointestinal symptoms, higher gut permeability markers (LPS, zonulin), elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6, TNF-α), and poorer sleep quality compared to day-shift workers. The findings suggest night-shift work is associated with disrupted gut health, systemic inflammation, and sleep disturbances, indicating a need for lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: A mechanism investigation on the effective strategy for alleviating acute myocardial infarction associated with sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: This study investigated the therapeutic effects of bisoprolol amlodipine tablet (BAT) combined with Shumian capsule (SMC) on myocardial injury in rats with acute myocardial infarction and sleep deprivation. The combination improved cardiac function, reduced inflammation and fibrosis, and suppressed Panx1/P2X7 pathway and NETosis-related markers, suggesting a novel strategy for AMI with insomnia.

papers.title: The stress-fascia-pain axis in myofascial pain syndrome: a mechanistic integrative review and conceptual synthesis.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on myofascial pain syndrome, proposing a stress-fascia-pain axis that integrates trigger-point biochemistry, fascial biomechanics, stress-related neuroendocrine changes, and central sensitization. The authors suggest this framework explains heterogeneity and supports multimodal treatment, though evidence strength varies across domains.

papers.title: Analysis of psychomotor latency, spatial reasoning, and metabolic health markers in adolescent gamers: A comparative study of the impact of the confounding triad of sleep, diet, and screen modality.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion
papers.summary: This comparative cross-sectional study of 200 male adolescents found that gamers had faster psychomotor reaction times and better spatial reasoning than non-gamers, with dose-dependent improvements from gaming hours, but poor sleep negatively impacted performance. Dietary caloric intake was a stronger predictor of adiposity than gaming, suggesting that metabolic risks are more related to diet than to gaming itself.

papers.title: New-Onset Convulsive Status Epilepticus Temporally Associated With Accidental Inhalation of Billygoat Weed (Ageratum conyzoides) Smoke: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report describes a 76-year-old man who developed new-onset convulsive status epilepticus shortly after inhaling smoke from burning Ageratum conyzoides (billygoat weed). Extensive workup revealed no other cause, and the patient recovered fully, suggesting a potential neurotoxic trigger.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Effects of Rauwolfia vomitoria Against 3-nitropropionic Acid-induced Motor Impairment and Oxidative Stress in Mice.
papers.summary: This study in mice examined the neuroprotective effects of Rauwolfia vomitoria against motor impairment and oxidative stress induced by 3-nitropropionic acid, a mitochondrial toxin. Treatment with the plant extract improved motor coordination and reduced oxidative stress markers, suggesting potential for movement disorder therapy.

papers.title: Biologically Driven In Vivo Occlusion Design Provides a Reliable Experimental Glaucoma Mouse Model
papers.summary: The authors developed an injectable Viscobeads platform with a polystyrene core and biodegradable viscoelastic shell to occlude the trabecular meshwork, providing sustained intraocular pressure elevation for at least 8 weeks in mice. This model led to a 34% loss of retinal ganglion cells and early dysfunction, supporting its use for studying glaucoma pathology and therapeutic evaluation.

papers.title: Withdrawal notice to "Corrigendum to Complement activation sustains neuroinflammation and deteriorates adult neurogenesis and spatial memory impairment in rat hippocampus following sleep deprivation" [Brain, Behav., Immun. 137 (2026) 106787].
papers.summary: This is a withdrawal notice for a corrigendum to a previously published article on complement activation and sleep deprivation effects.

papers.title: Paroxysmal tonic upgaze mimicking epileptic seizures in infancy: a diagnostic challenge.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 11-month-old infant with paroxysmal tonic upgaze, a non-epileptic disorder, highlighting its clinical features and the importance of recognizing it to avoid misdiagnosis of epilepsy.

papers.title: Machine learning and molecular docking-driven identification of novel umami peptides from pea protein and electroencephalography (EEG) neural mechanisms analysis of their umami-enhancing effects.
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and molecular docking to identify novel umami peptides from pea protein, including QEGEK, QEEEEQSH, and ATTETVDALR. EEG analysis showed that two peptides enhanced umami perception, with stronger neural oscillations in theta, alpha, and beta bands, and activation in parietal and parieto-occipital regions.

papers.title: Education Research: Development of a Workplace-Based Assessment to Enhance EEG Interpretation Skills for Medical Students.
papers.summary: The authors developed a workplace-based assessment (WBA) tool for EEG interpretation during a 2-week medical student elective. Over 79 WBAs with 20 students, they found a significant reduction in faculty assistance needed from week 1 to week 2, and high feasibility and educational value reported by students and faculty.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
